:::

This module runs automated data-quality checks (outliers, miscoded missing values, empty and constant columns, SPSS filter variables, category casing, problematic column names, mixed text encodings, spreadsheet formatting) on the extracted data files.
We examined 26 columns across 10 data files.
2 file/column combinations have at least one issue.

```{r} #| echo: false # table data -------------------------------------- table <- structure(list(File = c("na_strings.csv", "na_strings.csv"), Column = c("a", "c"), Issues = c("⬜ Empty column — Column is empty: all 2 values are missing", "⬜ Empty column — Column is empty: all 2 values are missing" )), row.names = c(NA, -2L), class = "data.frame") # display table ----------------------------------- metacheck::report_table(table, "auto", 20, FALSE) ```
No file could be screened for careless responding.

**What this does not cover.** Only 0 of 10 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

-  We classified 13 files: 12 data, 1 documentation.
-  We found 11 tabular data files and extracted 26 columns from 11 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1).
-  The study-group step did not get an answer for 13 files (the model request failed); they were grouped by the fallback rules instead.
-  1 trial-level data file (E-Prime / Inquisit / jsPsych / Behaverse) was recognised. These are per-participant records of a behavioural task, so they are not listed as separate datasets — convert_psychds() merges them per instrument into Behaverse `paradata/<instrument>.json` (one file per instrument, all participants). Nothing is deleted. We ran automated data-quality checks on 26 columns; 2 columns have at least one potential issue (2 columns with no observed values (entirely empty)).
